ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a transformer, the primary side is labeled u1, the secondary side is labeled u2, and the problem statement gives U2 = 10 V. The secondary side is connected to a bridge rectifier circuit composed of D1, D2, D3, and D4; the output terminal on the right side is connected to a filter capacitor C, a parallel load resistor RL, the output voltage is labeled u0, the capacitor voltage is labeled uc, and the load current is labeled i0. Reasoning: During normal bridge rectification, two diagonal diodes conduct in one half-cycle, and the other two diagonal diodes conduct in the other half-cycle, so both half-cycles can supply power to the capacitor and load. If D2 is open-circuited, then that half-cycle conduction path containing D2 is cut off, and the rectifier bridge cannot effectively charge the capacitor and load in both half-cycles, so the output average voltage and load current demand decrease. Therefore the average current flowing through D1 also becomes smaller accordingly. Conclusion: After D2 is open-circuited, the average current of D1 decreases.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: the transformer secondary u2=10 V supplies a diode bridge D1-D4, whose output is filtered by capacitor C and loaded by RL. In normal operation, opposite diode pairs conduct on alternate half-cycles to keep charging the capacitor and supplying the load. Then impose the text-stated fault: D2 is open-circuited. Because D2 is part of one alternate bridge conduction path, that path can no longer conduct, so the rectifier no longer supplies the load/capacitor on both half-cycles. The reduced charging opportunity lowers the DC output/load current demand, so the average current through D1 becomes smaller. Conclude: the average current through D1 decreases.
